brief.headline: Memory stocks in bear market as Samsung earnings disappoint despite record profit; HBM4 ramp vs pricing pressure at crossroads
brief.summary: <cite index="42-7,42-8,42-9">Samsung, SK Hynix, Micron, and memory ETF all down 20%+ from recent highs despite Samsung's record $59B operating profit estimate.</cite> <cite index="38-10">Samsung fell 9.06% to 286,000 won and SK Hynix dropped 14.57% to 2,187,000 won in recent session.</cite> <cite index="14-4">Conventional DRAM contract prices rose 93-98% QoQ in Q1 2026, but Q2 increases decelerated to 58-63%</cite> and <cite index="18-2">Q3 projected at 13-18%—first signs of cooling.</cite> <cite index="3-10,3-1">HBM3E accounts for ~66% of total HBM shipments in 2026 while HBM4 gradually ramps, with SK Hynix maintaining 50%+ share.</cite> <cite index="6-8">SK Hynix shipped 12-layer HBM4E samples to major customers in June,</cite> positioning for <cite index="5-7">Nvidia's Rubin platform launch in H2 2026.</cite>
brief.pair_trade_view: SK Hynix structurally advantaged. <cite index="3-12,3-11">SK holds 62% HBM shipment share (Q2 2025) and 57% revenue share (Q3),</cite> while <cite index="4-8">Samsung held 53% HBM market share in Q3 2025 versus Samsung's 35%.</cite> <cite index="3-18">UBS projects SK Hynix ~70% share of HBM4 for Nvidia Rubin platform in 2026.</cite> <cite index="6-8,6-9">SK Hynix shipped 12-layer HBM4E samples in June on schedule, delivering 16Gbps pin speeds with 20%+ power efficiency gains.</cite> Samsung messaging "customers say 'Samsung is back' on HBM4" but execution risk remains after HBM3E qualification delays. <cite index="38-11,38-12,38-13">SK Hynix announced 100 trillion won ($64B) investment including 80 trillion for M17 NAND fab (2029 start) and 20 trillion for P&T7 advanced packaging.</cite> Relative call: long SK Hynix vs Samsung on HBM4 qualification timing, TSMC packaging partnership depth, and narrower earnings multiple on same AI secular exposure.

memory_cycle.notes: <cite index="14-4">Q1 2026 conventional DRAM contract prices surged 93-98% QoQ—buyers paid double vs three months prior.</cite> <cite index="18-2">Q3 2026 projected at 13-18% increase (DRAM) and 10-15% (NAND)—substantial but marked slowdown.</cite> <cite index="14-17,14-19">Spot buyers stopped chasing higher quotes in June; NAND spot trading gone quiet even as headline numbers stay green.</cite> <cite index="13-27,13-28,13-30">2026 shortage is demand-driven (AI HBM consuming wafer capacity) vs 2021 supply disruption; demand-driven shortages persist as long as AI demand keeps growing.</cite> <cite index="15-3,15-4">Clear shortage expected in 2026, with meaningful capacity expansion unlikely until late 2027 or 2028; CSPs signing LTAs to secure stable supply at higher prices.</cite> <cite index="17-22,17-23">HBM crowding out commodity DRAM; Micron noted 3-to-1 conversion ratio (HBM to DDR5 wafer capacity).</cite> Pricing power intact but rate-of-change inflecting. Watch for contract price moderation in Q4 2026 data.

brief.hbm_pulse: <cite index="3-8,3-9,3-10">HBM3E remains flagship product in 2026; Google/AWS expanding proprietary ASIC dev selecting HBM3E; analysts expect HBM3E ~66% of total HBM shipments, HBM4 gradually increasing share.</cite> <cite index="6-8,6-9,6-10">SK Hynix shipped 12-layer HBM4E samples to major customers June 18; 16Gbps per pin, 20%+ power efficiency vs HBM4, 48GB capacity.</cite> <cite index="5-11,5-13,5-15">Nvidia reportedly inquired about 16-layer HBM for Q4 2026 delivery; performance evaluation expected before Q3 2026; transition from 12 to 16 layers pulling forward generational shift before 12-layer reaches full commercial rollout.</cite> <cite index="10-1,10-5">Micron in high volume production of HBM4 36GB 12H, achieving 11Gbps+ pin speeds enabling 2.8TB/s bandwidth, 2.3x bandwidth and 20%+ power efficiency vs HBM3E.</cite> <cite index="5-21">SK Hynix established HBM4 mass production framework and supplying paid samples to Nvidia.</cite> <cite index="4-1,4-5">Samsung in 'close discussion' to supply HBM4 to Nvidia; customers stating 'Samsung is back' on HBM4.</cite> <cite index="1-9">Some analysts warn HBM prices could enter correction phase after 2026 as competition heats up and capacity expands.</cite>

news_pulse.headline: Memory stocks enter bear market: Samsung, SK Hynix, Micron down 20%+ despite record Samsung profit
news_pulse.implication: Investor tolerance for memory premium valuations cracking despite fundamental shortage narrative. Samsung's $59B operating profit guide (+1,800% YoY) failed to satisfy—market pricing late-cycle dynamics. Semis basket lost $1.5T market cap since June 25.

news_pulse.headline: SK Hynix announces 100 trillion won ($64B) investment: 80T for M17 NAND fab, 20T for P&T7 packaging
news_pulse.implication: M17 NAND fab construction starts 2027, operations H1 2029. P&T7 packaging expansion targets HBM server DRAM and enterprise SSD demand. Signals confidence in sustained AI-driven memory demand through end of decade, but 3-year lead time limits near-term supply response.

news_pulse.headline: SK Hynix ships 12-layer HBM4E samples to major customers; 16Gbps, 20%+ power efficiency gain
news_pulse.implication: On-schedule delivery reinforces SK's HBM leadership. 48GB capacity 12-layer stack uses Advanced MR-MUF, 17% better heat resistance vs HBM4. Supports Nvidia Rubin (H2 2026) and positions for 16-layer pull-in if Nvidia inquiry materializes.

news_pulse.headline: Nvidia inquires about 16-layer HBM delivery Q4 2026; exploratory, no contracts signed
news_pulse.implication: Nvidia pulling forward generational roadmap before 12-layer HBM4 reaches full commercial rollout. 16-layer 'much harder' than 8-to-12 transition—process itself must change. Performance eval expected before Q3 2026. Intensifies qualification pressure on Samsung vs SK Hynix/Micron.

news_pulse.headline: TSMC CoWoS supply-demand gap narrowing from 20% to 10% by end-2026; 60%+ capacity expansion by 2027
news_pulse.implication: Advanced packaging bottleneck easing but still tight. TSMC CoWoS capacity forecast 80%+ CAGR 2022-2027. CoWoS-L orders from Nvidia B200/Rubin and AMD MI400 driving expansion. CoPoS pilot production mid-2027. Modest relief for HBM supply chain by late 2026.

news_pulse.headline: Conventional DRAM contract prices +13-18% QoQ in Q3 2026 (vs +58-63% Q2, +93-98% Q1); NAND +10-15%
news_pulse.implication: Rate-of-change inflecting as consumer buyers hit affordability ceiling. Spot buyers stopped chasing higher quotes in June. Server/AI demand still tight but pricing power moderating. First sign of plateau—not reversal—but confirms parabolic phase maturing.

news_pulse.headline: Hyperscaler 2026 capex estimates: $602B-$725B, up 36-77% YoY; ~75% allocated to AI infrastructure
news_pulse.implication: Amazon ~$200B, Microsoft $120B+, Alphabet $175-185B, Meta $125-145B (raised from $115-135B). Oracle $50B. Consensus repeatedly too low (2024-2025 both exceeded 50% vs 20% estimates). Goldman: $200B upside risk to 2026 estimates. Memory demand structurally supported but investor patience for capex returns waning.

news_pulse.headline: US Commerce Secretary Lutnick presses Samsung, SK Hynix to expand US memory production for AI
news_pulse.implication: Geopolitical pressure for US memory fab capacity intensifying. Discussions confirmed but no specifics disclosed. Could accelerate CHIPS Act funding for Korean memory makers' US expansions, but lead times remain 3-4 years. Near-term supply picture unchanged.

brief.derivatives_signal: Elevated vol post-selloff. Memory stocks whipsawed—bear market entry despite record fundamentals signals macro/multiple compression vs demand destruction. Options skew likely elevated on downside after -20% drawdowns. SK Hynix US ADR listing (recent) adds liquidity but watch basis vs KRX 000660. Samsung 005930 support at 280K-285K tested; SK Hynix 000660 at 2.1-2.2M range. KOSPI Composite correlation to Nasdaq increasing. Near-term tactical: sell rallies into Q3 earnings unless memory pricing data stabilizes. Longer-term structural call on HBM remains intact—use pullback to add SK Hynix on 12-18 month view if ADR liquidity improves. Pair trade: long SK Hynix ADR vs Samsung ADR (or vs MU) captures HBM4 qualification gap and TSMC packaging allocation advantage.
watch_for_next_3h: Any Samsung or SK Hynix official commentary on HBM4 qualification status or Nvidia Rubin design-win confirmation
TrendForce or DRAMeXchange spot pricing updates (DDR4/DDR5 8Gb, 512Gb NAND) for week of July 13
TSMC supply chain commentary on CoWoS allocation or CoPoS pilot line progress
Hyperscaler earnings commentary on memory cost inflation and AI capex sustainability (watch for Meta, Alphabet guidance revisions)
Korean won FX moves vs USD (USDKRW) and KOSPI futures—memory stocks sensitive to macro risk-off and export competitiveness
